title: VCRI Processes Asset Assessment Methodology v1

grades.meaning: Best-in-class process posture. Documented, owned, enforced, and measured processes with segregation of duties and continuous improvement across all dimensions. No critical findings.
Solid process posture. Documented and owned processes across most dimensions; minor gaps in 1-2 areas with remediation paths defined. Suitable for production reliance with stated caveats.
Acceptable with conditions. Notable gaps in 2-3 dimensions; remediation roadmap required. Not suitable for high-assurance reliance without compensating controls.
Significant gaps across multiple dimensions. Operational risk is material; remediation required before high-assurance reliance.
Material failure of process posture. Tribal knowledge and ad-hoc execution dominate; reliance not recommended in current state.

subcriteria.title: Process documentation and standardization
anchors: No process documentation; procedures are tribal knowledge held by individuals.
Some processes documented ad-hoc; documentation is partial, stale, and inconsistent.
A documentation standard is defined but inconsistently applied; key processes remain undocumented.
In-scope processes documented to a consistent standard and kept current; runbooks exist for operational procedures.
All of #3 plus a managed process framework, periodic documentation review, and audited coverage of in-scope processes.
All of #4 plus a continuously maintained, org-wide standardized process library with independently validated completeness.

subcriteria.title: Process ownership and accountability
anchors: No process owners; responsibility for any given process is unclear.
Ownership assumed informally for some processes; many have no named owner.
An ownership model is defined but inconsistently assigned; gaps and overlaps persist.
Every in-scope process has a documented, accountable owner consistently maintained.
All of #3 plus owner performance/accountability measured, escalation paths defined, and audited ownership currency.
All of #4 plus org-wide ownership governance with independently attested accountability.

subcriteria.title: Process change provenance and version control
anchors: Process changes happen without record; no history of who changed what or why.
Some changes noted ad-hoc; no version control or rationale capture.
A change-provenance standard is defined but inconsistently followed; history is incomplete.
Process changes consistently version-controlled with author, date, and rationale captured.
All of #3 plus enforced change provenance integrated with approval workflow and audited history integrity.
All of #4 plus cryptographically attested, immutable process-change provenance independently verifiable.

subcriteria.title: Process ownership-to-role mapping and RACI
anchors: No RACI or role mapping; it is unclear who is responsible, accountable, consulted, or informed.
RACI exists informally for a few processes; mostly undefined.
A RACI standard is defined but inconsistently applied; roles drift from reality.
Documented RACI consistently maintained for in-scope processes; roles mapped to verified identities.
All of #3 plus automated workflow routing tied to roles and audited RACI accuracy.
All of #4 plus continuously governed role-to-process mapping with independently attested accuracy.

subcriteria.title: Step-level attribution to verified identity
anchors: Process steps cannot be attributed to a specific actor; execution is anonymous.
Some steps logged to a user ad-hoc; attribution is partial and unreliable.
An attribution standard is defined but inconsistently captured across process steps.
In-scope process steps consistently attributed to verified identities with logged execution.
All of #3 plus enforced identity verification at each consequential step and audited attribution completeness.
All of #4 plus cryptographically attributable step execution independently verifiable.

subcriteria.title: Non-repudiation on approvals
anchors: Approvals are informal and deniable; no record binds an approver to a decision.
Approvals captured ad-hoc (email, verbal); no consistent non-repudiation.
An approval-record standard is defined but inconsistently applied; integrity is weak.
Approvals consistently recorded and attributable to the approving identity for in-scope processes.
All of #3 plus tamper-resistant approval records integrated with workflow and audited integrity.
All of #4 plus digitally signed, non-repudiable approvals with independently verifiable integrity.

subcriteria.title: Privacy impact assessment in process design
anchors: New or changed processes are deployed with no privacy review.
Privacy considered informally for some high-risk processes; no defined trigger.
A PIA requirement is defined but inconsistently performed before process deployment.
Documented PIA consistently performed before deploying or materially changing in-scope processes.
All of #3 plus automated PIA triggers on process changes and audited PIA completion/quality.
All of #4 plus continuous privacy-by-design enforcement in process creation with independently validated coverage.

subcriteria.title: Data minimization in workflows
anchors: Workflows collect and pass whatever data is convenient, without minimization.
Minimization applied ad-hoc in some workflows; no standard.
A minimization standard for workflow design is defined but inconsistently applied.
Data minimization documented and consistently applied in in-scope workflow design.
All of #3 plus measured data-handled-vs-necessary per workflow and audited minimization adherence.
All of #4 plus self-minimizing workflows with independently validated minimization.

subcriteria.title: Privacy-by-design in process templates
anchors: Process templates contain no privacy controls; privacy is an afterthought.
A few templates mention privacy ad-hoc; no consistent embedding.
Privacy-by-design template requirements are defined but inconsistently embedded.
Privacy controls consistently embedded in in-scope process templates and reused.
All of #3 plus enforced privacy-by-design template gates and audited template compliance.
All of #4 plus continuously improved privacy-by-design templates with independently validated effectiveness.

subcriteria.title: Segregation of duties and approval gates
anchors: No segregation of duties; a single actor can initiate, approve, and execute sensitive actions.
SoD and approvals applied ad-hoc where compliance forces it; broad gaps remain.
An SoD/approval-gate standard is defined but inconsistently enforced across sensitive processes.
Segregation of duties and approval gates documented and consistently enforced for in-scope sensitive processes.
All of #3 plus automated SoD-violation detection, enforced approval routing, and audited control adherence.
All of #4 plus continuous SoD monitoring and independently attested control enforcement.

subcriteria.title: Process control framework
anchors: No process control framework; controls, if any, are uncoordinated.
Some controls exist ad-hoc; no framework mapping controls to risks.
A control framework is defined but inconsistently implemented; coverage is partial.
A documented process control framework consistently implemented across in-scope processes.
All of #3 plus controls mapped to risks, control testing on a cadence, and audited framework coverage.
All of #4 plus a self-improving control framework with independently attested control design and operation.

subcriteria.title: Process exception and deviation handling
anchors: Process deviations happen silently; exceptions are neither tracked nor reviewed.
Exceptions handled ad-hoc; no consistent record or approval.
An exception-handling standard is defined but inconsistently followed; deviations under-recorded.
Documented exception/deviation handling consistently applied; exceptions approved and tracked.
All of #3 plus automated deviation detection with risk scoring and audited exception closure.
All of #4 plus continuous deviation analytics driving process hardening, independently validated.

subcriteria.title: Change management
anchors: Changes to systems and processes happen without change control; outages from unmanaged change are common.
Change tracked ad-hoc in tickets; no consistent review or approval.
A change-management standard is defined but inconsistently followed; emergency changes bypass it.
Documented change management (request, review, approval, rollback) consistently applied to in-scope changes.
All of #3 plus a change advisory function, measured change-success/incident rates, and audited change adherence.
All of #4 plus continuously improved, largely automated change governance with independently validated effectiveness.

subcriteria.title: Business continuity and process recovery
anchors: No continuity planning; a disruption halts critical processes indefinitely.
Continuity considered informally; no documented plan or recovery objectives.
A continuity/recovery standard with objectives is defined but inconsistently maintained and untested.
Documented business-continuity plans with recovery objectives consistently maintained for critical in-scope processes.
All of #3 plus tested continuity (exercises), measured recovery against objectives, and audited plan currency.
All of #4 plus regularly exercised, resilient continuity with independently validated recovery performance.

subcriteria.title: Process integrity and deviation detection
anchors: No assurance that processes execute as designed; silent process failures go unnoticed.
Process correctness checked ad-hoc and manually; no standard.
A process-integrity standard is defined but inconsistently applied; monitoring is sparse.
Process integrity verified consistently for in-scope processes (defined checks that the process did what it should).
All of #3 plus automated detection of process deviation/failure with alerting and audited integrity coverage.
All of #4 plus process mining and continuous integrity analytics with independently validated assurance.

subcriteria.title: Process control monitoring
anchors: Process-control execution is not monitored; nobody knows if controls are running.
Some control execution observed ad-hoc; no consistent monitoring.
A control-monitoring standard is defined but inconsistently applied; coverage has gaps.
Process-control execution consistently monitored and recorded for in-scope processes.
All of #3 plus alerting on control failures/bypass, with monitoring coverage audited.
All of #4 plus continuous, analytics-driven control monitoring with independently validated coverage.

subcriteria.title: Control effectiveness measurement and audit
anchors: Control effectiveness is never measured; controls are assumed to work.
Effectiveness reviewed ad-hoc; no metrics or schedule.
An effectiveness-measurement standard is defined but inconsistently executed.
Control effectiveness consistently measured and internally audited on a defined cadence.
All of #3 plus quantified control-effectiveness metrics, deviation risk scoring, and tracked remediation.
All of #4 plus independent (external) audit of control effectiveness with attested results.

subcriteria.title: Continuous process improvement and mining
anchors: Processes are never reviewed for improvement; inefficiency and risk accumulate.
Improvement happens reactively after incidents only; no systematic review.
A process-improvement standard is defined but inconsistently applied.
Documented continuous-improvement practice consistently applied to in-scope processes.
All of #3 plus data-driven improvement (process mining/metrics) and audited improvement outcomes.
All of #4 plus self-optimizing processes with automated improvement recommendations, independently validated.
